title: Diagnose and recover PostgreSQL connection exhaustion
trigger: New application database connections fail with remaining-connection-slots or too-many-clients errors while PostgreSQL may still answer existing or reserved administrative sessions.
preconditions: confirm whether any administrative or existing PostgreSQL connection remains available
capture max_connections, superuser_reserved_connections, and reserved_connections when present
identify session ownership and application_name distribution in pg_stat_activity
reproduce the failure with an ordinary non-superuser application connection
confirm the problem is connection-slot capacity rather than authentication, network, lock, or query latency
obtain approval before terminating application sessions
diagnostic_steps: compare current client-session usage with max_connections and reserved connection settings
group pg_stat_activity by application_name, user, and state to locate dominant consumers
confirm a non-superuser probe fails with a connection-slot exhaustion error
confirm the reserved administrative path remains usable if available
check recent deployment, autoscaling, connection-pool, retry, and timeout changes
look for idle or unexpectedly duplicated application sessions that explain capacity growth
mitigation_steps: release the smallest safe number of known offending application sessions needed to restore ordinary capacity
prefer evidence-matched session termination or application-pool remediation over restarting PostgreSQL
do not raise max_connections during an incident without DBA/resource review because each additional backend consumes memory and server resources
do not mass-terminate unrelated sessions solely to make the connection count decrease
validation_steps: a fresh ordinary application connection succeeds
PostgreSQL remains reachable through the administrative path
pg_stat_activity shows ordinary capacity below the exhaustion boundary
customer/API connection acquisition recovers where applicable
retain connection-setting and session-distribution evidence for problem review
escalation_boundary: Escalate to DBA/application ownership when the dominant sessions are business-critical or unidentified, reserved administrative capacity is unavailable, saturation immediately recurs, pool/retry behavior needs code or configuration change, or max_connections/resource sizing must be changed.
